assumptions: The initial product covers a tightly bounded Polish-led workflow and at most one or two additional national regimes rather than promising comprehensive EU legal coverage.
Future PPWR fee and recyclability outputs are clearly labelled scenarios until the relevant delegated and implementing acts are final.
Customers retain legal responsibility and perform required filings; the product supplies governed evidence, approvals, and exports rather than legal advice or delegated filing.
The founder uses no confidential Reckitt information, supplier terms, work time, or employer relationships without permission.
Pricing, gross margin, retention, savings, channel conversion, and the 180-group growth path remain unvalidated commercial hypotheses.

factors.name: Core insight
factors.rationale: The opportunity correctly moves upstream from free filing portals and generic calculators to the changing packaging BOM, supplier evidence, approval history, and country mappings that determine report quality. PPWR transition and differentiated national rules make that control point recurrent.

factors.name: Customer pain and willingness to pay
factors.rationale: Verifiable component material and weight data, recurring packaging changes, and multi-country obligations create credible operational pain for multi-SKU brands. Paid demand for governed change control is unobserved, while free portals and low-priced compliance products make a premium budget uncertain.

factors.name: Business model and economics
factors.rationale: Onboarding plus recurring workspace and revision fees can produce recurring revenue, and a scoped pilot fits available capital. Proposed monthly prices exceed some published self-serve anchors, while specialist rule maintenance, supplier support, extraction review, multi-country expansion, unproven retention, and channel CAC weaken the otherwise plausible margin profile.

factors.name: Market and beachhead
factors.rationale: Mid-market multi-SKU consumer brands selling across several EU countries are a coherent segment with repeat packaging-data work, and Poland offers an accessible starting market. The beachhead still needs sharper vertical and country boundaries, but the EU-wide adjacency can support meaningful scale.

factors.name: Competitive position and domination potential
factors.rationale: Approval workflow, source provenance, and supplier collaboration distinguish the concept from a bare calculator or filing interface. Direct products already advertise declarations, grades, EPR market sheets, APIs, and mid-market FMCG coverage, so domination requires owning a much narrower workflow rather than matching feature lists.

factors.name: Expansion potential
factors.rationale: Winning one packaging-intensive segment can extend across countries, suppliers, packaging categories, design approvals, procurement, and related product-information or sustainability evidence. Each jurisdiction adds maintenance cost, so expansion is attractive but not frictionless.

factors.name: Defensibility and durability
factors.rationale: A versioned evidence graph embedded in supplier requests and approval decisions can accumulate reusable classifications, correction patterns, and switching costs. Regulations and fee tables are public, cross-customer data rights are unclear, and competitors can replicate workflow features, leaving only moderate durability.

factors.name: Strength of advantage
factors.rationale: Moving compliance checks before procurement and retaining verifiable evidence could prevent rework and make changes faster and safer. There is no measured reduction in redesigns, reporting corrections, analyst time, or approval cycle time, so the behavioral and economic advantage remains plausible rather than demonstrated.

factors.name: Timing and momentum
factors.rationale: PPWR's 2026 general application and the coexistence of differentiated national EPR regimes create an immediate transition window for packaging-data cleanup and governance. Later recyclability and fee-modulation acts also make authoritative long-range simulation premature, so timing favors evidence readiness more than definitive forecasting.

factors.name: Distribution
factors.rationale: Converters, design agencies, EPR advisers, fractional sustainability teams, and product-information implementers can aggregate relevant customers. There are no partner commitments, converters may resist substitution recommendations, and the founder must avoid relying on employer-derived access, leaving repeatable CAC unresolved.

factors.name: Execution and risks
factors.rationale: The founder's FMCG context, data skills, document automation capability, and Polish base fit a bounded pilot that can run within the stated time and capital. Supplier incompleteness, legal-interpretation boundaries, rule freshness, multi-country specialist review, and employment conflicts become substantial at scale but are delegable rather than inherently prohibitive.

main_structural_strength: The product can sit at the approved packaging specification and evidence pack before procurement and reporting, turning recurring supplier and country data changes into a workflow system rather than an episodic filing tool.
primary_score_limiter: It has not established that brands will pay a durable premium for governed change control above low-cost compliance trackers and free official portals, especially when supplier evidence may remain incomplete.
strongest_disconfirming_evidence: PPWR Connect and PackComply already advertise overlapping functions at EUR 29 to EUR 299 per month, while key PPWR grading and fee-modulation methods still depend on future acts, undermining both near-term differentiation and authoritative simulation.
evidence_needed_for_higher_score: Three paid pilots in a sharply defined packaging segment should document supplier response and BOM completeness, at least one avoided correction or redesign or a measured 25 to 60 hours saved, renewal intent at the proposed price, and a converter or EPR-adviser channel willing to bring additional accounts.
highest_value_structural_change: Narrow the wedge to the packaging-change approval system for one high-change consumer category trading across a fixed two-country corridor, delivered through an EPR adviser or design partner; make country exports a by-product of the governed supplier-evidence workflow rather than the core product.
